inventedEvidence.evidence: 'Because the brush bar is still tight even after you've cleared some debris' - the customer had only said it was tight with hair and a tassel wrapped round it; they had not cleared anything yet

rationale: The assistant ultimately reached the correct cause (brushbar jam snapped the drive belt) and recommended the right part with the model established, but only because the customer prompted the belt check after the assistant prematurely wrapped up with 'Is there anything else I can assist you with today?'. It over-escalated a classic belt-friction smell into a fire-risk 'Stop using this appliance... until it has been checked by a qualified engineer', then contradicted that banner on every turn by guiding a DIY repair. It also invented that the customer had 'cleared some debris' before they had done so. Safe instructions (unplug first) were given, so a UK homeowner would get to the fix, albeit with confusing and inconsistent safety messaging.
